Visa is a world leader in digital payments, facilitating more than 215 billion payments transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories each year. Our mission is to connect the world through the most innovative, convenient, reliable and secure payments network, enabling individuals, businesses and economies to thrive.

When you join Visa, you join a culture of purpose and belonging – where your growth is priority, your identity is embraced, and the work you do matters. We believe that economies that include everyone everywhere, uplift everyone everywhere. Your work will have a direct impact on billions of people around the world – helping unlock financial access to enable the future of money movement.

Join Visa: A Network Working for Everyone.

Job Description

Payments are a very exciting and fast-developing area with a lot of new and innovative ideas coming to market. With strong demand for new solutions in this space, it promises to be an exciting area of innovation. VISA is a strong leader in the payment industry and is rapidly transitioning into a technology company with significant investments in this area.

If you want to be in the exciting payment space, learn fast and make big impacts, Ecosystem & Operational Risk technology which is part of Visa’s Value-Added Services business unit is an ideal place for you!

In Ecosystem & Operational Risk group, Payment Fraud Disruption team is responsible for building critical risk and fraud detection and prevention applications and services at Visa. This includes idea generation, architecture, design, development, and testing of products, applications, and services that provide Visa clients with solutions to detect, prevent, and mitigate fraud for Visa and Visa client payment systems.

This position is ideal for an experienced ML Engineer who is passionate about collaborating with business and technology partners in solving challenging fraud prevention problems. You will be a key driver in the effort to define the shared strategic vision for the Payment Fraud Disruption platform and defining tools and services that safeguard Visa’s payment systems. 

The candidate for this role need to have strong ML and Data Science background, with demonstrated experience in building, training, implementing and optimized advanced AI models for payments, risk or fraud prevention products that created business value and delivered impact within the payments or payments risk domain or have experience building AI/ML solutions for similar industries. 

To be successful in this role, the candidate need to be a technical leader with the ability to engage in high bandwidth conversations with business and technology partners and be able to think broadly about Visa’s business and drive solutions that will enhance the safety and integrity of Visa’s payment ecosystem. The candidate will help deliver innovative insights to Visa's strategic products and business. This role represents an exciting opportunity to make key contributions to strategic offering for Visa. This candidate needs to have strong academic track record and be able to demonstrate excellent software engineering skills. The candidate will be a self-starter comfortable with ambiguity, with strong attention to detail, and excellent collaboration skills.

• Present technical solutions, capabilities, considerations, and features in business terms. Effectively communicate status, issues, and risks in a precise and timely manner.
• Coaching and mentoring junior team members and evolving team talent pipeline.

This is a hybrid position. Hybrid employees can alternate time between both remote and office. Employees in hybrid roles are expected to work from the office 2-3 set days a week (determined by leadership/site), with a general guidepost of being in the office 50% or more of the time based on business needs.

• 8+ years of relevant work experience with a Bachelor’s Degree or at least 5 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g. Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or 2 years of work experience with a PhD, OR 11+ years of relevant work experience.

Project Brief: Development of a Machine Learning-Based Patent Data Mining and Filtering Application

Objective

To develop a machine learning (ML) application capable of mining patent databases, extracting relevant information, and filtering this data for display on a Python-based web application. This tool will enhance the ability to discover and analyze patent data efficiently, supporting better decision-making for patent research and development activities.

Scope

Data Acquisition: Connect to multiple patent databases to retrieve comprehensive patent information. This will involve establishing API connections or scraping data where APIs are unavailable.

Data Processing: Implement ML algorithms to process and analyze the raw data. The processing steps will include data cleaning, normalization, and transformation to ensure data quality and usability.

Development: Design and train ML models to identify and classify relevant patent data based on predefined criteria such as technology fields, novelty, and applicability.

Implementation: Integrate the ML models into the data pipeline to automatically filter and prioritize patents based on their potential value and relevance.

Backend: Develop a Python-based backend (using frameworks such as Django or Flask) to manage data flow, ML model integration, and API endpoints.

Frontend: Create a user-friendly interface that allows users to specify search criteria, display filtered patents, and interact with the data.

Testing and Validation: Conduct comprehensive testing to ensure the application's functionality, performance, and accuracy in filtering and presenting data.

Deployment and Maintenance:

Deployment: Deploy the web application on a suitable cloud platform to ensure scalability and accessibility.

Maintenance: Establish procedures for regular updates to ML models and database connections to adapt to new patent filings and evolving data standards.

Deliverables

ML Model Documentation and Code: Complete documentation of the model development process, including data schemas, algorithm choices, and training methodologies.

Web Application Codebase: Fully documented and tested code for both the backend and frontend components.

Deployment Guide: Instructions for deploying and maintaining the web application, including environment setup, scaling strategies, and security measures.

User Manual: A comprehensive guide for end-users on how to navigate and use the web application effectively.

Job Description:

Vehicle Re-identification

Vehicle re-identification (Re-ID) is a computer vision task that aims to match vehicle images captured from non-overlapping camera views. The goal is to identify the same vehicle instance across multiple camera views, which can be useful for traffic management and law enforcement applications. Vehicle Re-ID has several challenges, including variations in viewpoint, illumination, occlusion, and camera hardware differences. Researchers have proposed various approaches to tackle these challenges, including deep learning-based methods that leverage powerful feature representations to match similar vehicles. The performance of vehicle Re-ID has improved significantly in recent years, but it remains an active area of research due to its practical importance and technical difficulty.

The purpose of this coursework is to gain real-world development experience in design, training, and evaluation of a Convolution Neural Network (CNN) for vehicle Re-ID. This will be achieved through the Google Colab with PyTorch as the framework.

1. Project Overview

Objective: To verify phone numbers by making automated calls where the recipient confirms their name. The system updates the user's status in the database based on their confirmation.

2. Required Tools and Technologies

a. Telecommunication Provider

Twilio: Offers robust APIs for making phone calls and sending SMS. Twilio’s Programmable Voice lets you make automated calls and interact with users via voice commands.

Nexmo (Vonage): Another service that provides APIs for voice and messaging services, suitable for initiating calls and processing interactions.

b. AI and Voice Recognition

Google Cloud Speech-to-Text: Converts audio (the recipient's spoken name) into text data. Useful for understanding user responses during the call.

IBM Watson Speech to Text: Provides an alternative to Google's service with similar capabilities.

c. Application Programming Interface (API) Management

Node.js/Express: For building the backend service that handles API requests and integrates with Twilio or Nexmo and the AI services.

Python with Flask or Django: As an alternative to Node.js, Python frameworks can also be used to manage backend logic and APIs.

d. Database Management

MySQL/PostgreSQL: To store user data and call dispositions.

MongoDB: A NoSQL alternative if the data structure is more flexible or document-oriented.

e. Front-end Development (Optional)

ReactJS/Angular: For building any administrative front-end interfaces for monitoring calls and managing data.

Bootstrap/Material-UI: Frameworks for quick UI development if required.

3. Workflow Description

Initiate Call: Using Twilio or Nexmo, the system makes an automated call to the user’s phone number.

Voice Interaction: The bot asks the recipient to confirm their name. This interaction is powered by the chosen speech-to-text AI technology.

Process Response: The AI interprets the spoken response and converts it into text.

Verify and Update Database: The backend system verifies the response against the database. If the user confirms their name correctly, the database is updated with the new disposition.

4. Security and Compliance

Data Protection: Ensure compliance with data protection regulations such as GDPR or HIPAA as applicable.

Secure API Usage: Use HTTPS for all API interactions and secure keys and credentials properly.

5. Development and Deployment

Version Control: Use Git for version control.

Deployment: Deploy the application on cloud platforms like AWS, Google Cloud, or Heroku.

6. Testing and Quality Assurance

Unit Testing: Use frameworks like Jest (for Node.js) or PyTest (for Python) to write and run tests.

Integration Testing: Test integration points between the telecommunication API, AI services, and the backend.

7. Maintenance and Monitoring

Logging and Monitoring: Use tools like Splunk, Datadog, or AWS CloudWatch to monitor the application's performance and log system activities.

This project requires a blend of telecommunication technologies, AI for voice recognition, and robust backend systems to manage the interactions and data. The choice of specific tools and technologies may vary based on budget, technical expertise, and specific project requirements.

Overview and Purpose:

We are seeking a Research Scientist for the Multimodal Data Analytics group in the Computational Science and Engineering Division (CSED).
